title: Navarin d'Agneau
subtitle: French spring lamb stew with peas, turnips and new potatoes
excerpt: Navarin d'agneau printanier is the great spring stew of France: lamb braised with early-season vegetables -- peas, green beans, small turnips, and new potatoes. It is gentler and lighter than a winter braise, finished with a clear, herby sauce rather than a rich reduced one. It is one of the most important dishes in the French spring repertoire.
sourceNotes: Navarin d'agneau printanier (spring lamb stew) is a classic of French home cooking. Printanier means 'spring' and refers to the use of the first vegetables of the season. The dish is traditionally made with lamb shoulder or neck. The sauce is thinner and clearer than a bourguignon -- finished with a small amount of stock and the juices from the lamb, not reduced wine.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The lamb can be braised up to the point of adding the spring vegetables. Add the vegetables when reheating.

content.text: The spring vegetables go in for the last 20 minutes only. If they cook too long they become grey and mushy. The lamb needs 1.5 hours in the oven before they are added. The finished dish should have a clear, flavourful sauce -- not thick, not reduced to a glaze.

Preheat the oven to 160C. Season {{lamb-shoulder}} lamb with {{salt-table}} salt and {{black-pepper}} pepper. Heat {{extra-virgin-olive-oil}} oil in a large ovenproof pot over high heat. Brown the lamb in batches, about 5 minutes per batch. Remove and set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Add {{onion}} onion and cook for 5 minutes. Add {{garlic}} garlic, {{tomato-puree}} tomato puree, and {{plain-flour}} flour. Stir for 1 minute. Pour in {{white-wine-dry}} wine and {{chicken-stock}} stock. Return the lamb with {{thyme-fresh}} thyme and {{bay-leaves}} bay leaves. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook in the oven for 1 hour.

Add {{turnip}} turnips and {{potatoes-waxy}} potatoes. Continue cooking for 30 minutes. Add {{peas-frozen}} peas and {{green-beans}} green beans. Cook for a further 10 minutes. Scatter {{parsley-flat}} parsley over and serve with bread.

items.symptom: The spring vegetables are overcooked and mushy
items.fix: Add peas and green beans only for the final 8 to 10 minutes. They need very little time. The turnips and potatoes go in earlier because they take longer, but should not cook for more than 30 minutes.

content.text: Navarin printanier is the dish that marks the end of winter in French cooking. It was traditionally made in April and May when the first young vegetables arrived in the market. It is a dish of French home cooking rather than restaurants -- the spring vegetables are too delicate and too precisely timed to work well in a commercial kitchen. It is made in homes across France every spring.
